faqs: FAQ
HOME
Frequently Asked Questions?
What are the early signs of gum disease?

Early signs of gum disease include red, swollen, or bleeding gums, persistent bad breath, gum tenderness, and gum recession. Scheduling a dental examination early can help prevent the condition from progressing and protect your long-term oral health.
When should wisdom teeth be removed?

Wisdom teeth may need removal if they are impacted, cause pain, crowd nearby teeth, or increase the risk of infection. Your dentist can evaluate your wisdom teeth and recommend treatment based on your individual oral health needs.
What is the difference between a dental crown and a dental filling?

A dental filling repairs small cavities or minor tooth damage, while a dental crown covers and strengthens a severely damaged or weakened tooth. Your dentist will recommend the most appropriate treatment after examining your tooth.
How can I reduce tooth sensitivity?

Tooth sensitivity may improve by using toothpaste designed for sensitive teeth, avoiding acidic foods, practicing proper brushing techniques, and visiting your dentist to identify and treat the underlying cause.
Can missing teeth affect my oral health?

Yes. Missing teeth can affect your bite, chewing ability, speech, and jawbone health. Replacing missing teeth with appropriate dental treatments helps maintain proper oral function and supports long-term dental health.
Why is preventive dental care important?

Preventive dental care helps reduce the risk of cavities, gum disease, and other oral health problems through routine examinations, professional cleanings, and early diagnosis, supporting healthier teeth and gums over time.

tooth-colored-restorations: Tooth-colored restorations repair teeth affected by cavities, minor chips, cracks, or wear while preserving a natural-looking smile. Each restoration is shaped and polished to support comfortable function, a balanced bite, and a seamless appearance.
Restore Strength Without a Metallic Look

Composite restorations bond directly to the tooth and can often be placed while preserving more of its healthy structure. Their natural shade makes them a discreet option for restoring visible teeth as well as many areas used for everyday biting and chewing.

Your treatment begins with an assessment of the affected tooth and surrounding tissues. After removing damaged or decayed material, we select a suitable shade, place the composite in precise layers, and carefully shape the restoration to complement your tooth.

A composite shade is selected to closely complement your natural enamel, helping the finished restoration blend with the surrounding tooth and maintain a balanced, natural-looking appearance.
The prepared tooth is carefully cleaned before the composite material is placed, shaped, and hardened in layers to rebuild the damaged area while supporting the remaining healthy structure.
We check your bite and make necessary adjustments before polishing the restoration. This final step helps create a smooth surface and promotes comfortable biting and chewing.

Tooth-colored restorations offer a practical way to address cavities and minor dental damage without drawing attention to the repaired area. With consistent brushing, flossing, professional cleanings, and mindful habits, your restoration can continue supporting your smile for years. Our team will explain how to care for the treated tooth and when it should be monitored.

dental-implants: A Lasting Foundation for Your Smile

Dental implants offer a stable, natural-looking way to replace one or more missing teeth. An implant is placed in the jawbone to support a custom dental crown, bridge, or other suitable restoration. At The Dental Hauz, we carefully assess your oral health and discuss your options to create a personalized treatment plan focused on comfort, function, appearance, and long-term care.

Missing teeth can affect chewing, speech, appearance, and the alignment of surrounding teeth. Dental implants are designed to provide dependable support without relying entirely on adjacent teeth. Once restored, an implant can look and function much like a natural tooth.

Every implant journey begins with a detailed examination and appropriate diagnostic imaging. We evaluate your teeth, gums, bite, and available bone before discussing your suitability, treatment stages, expected healing, and restoration options in clear, straightforward language.
What to Expect from Dental Implant Treatment
We examine your oral health and use appropriate imaging to assess the implant site, surrounding teeth, gums, and available bone before determining whether dental implants are suitable for you.
Your treatment plan considers the number and location of missing teeth, your overall oral health, restorative needs, and personal goals to support a functional and natural-looking result.
The dental implant is carefully positioned in the jawbone. A healing period generally follows, allowing the implant to integrate and form a stable foundation for the planned dental restoration.
Once the implant is ready, a custom crown, bridge, or other suitable restoration is attached. We carefully evaluate its shape, colour, fit, and bite for comfortable everyday function.
Protect and Maintain Your Dental Implant

Dental implants require consistent care, just like natural teeth. Daily brushing, cleaning around the implant, professional dental visits, and healthy habits help protect the surrounding gums and supporting structures. Our team will provide personalized maintenance guidance and monitor your implant during routine examinations to help support its condition over time.
We explain each stage of implant treatment so you know what to expect. Our approach emphasizes careful planning, honest guidance, comfortable care, and a restoration suited to your individual smile.

Relieve Discomfort and Preserve Your Tooth
Root Canal Therapy in Markham, ON

Root canal therapy is used to treat infection or inflammation inside a tooth while preserving as much of its natural structure as possible. When the inner pulp becomes affected by deep decay, trauma, or cracks, treatment may help protect the tooth from further damage. At The Dental Hauz, we carefully assess your condition and explain every step of your recommended care.
Saving a Natural Tooth

When appropriate, root canal therapy can remove infected or damaged tissue from inside the tooth, clean the root canals, and seal the space. The tooth is then restored to help support comfortable function.

Before treatment, we review your symptoms, examine the affected tooth, and use diagnostic imaging when needed. We explain the process, restoration needs, and follow-up care in clear, easy-to-understand language.

What to Expect During Root Canal Treatment
Detailed Diagnosis
We examine the tooth and surrounding area to understand the source of concern and determine whether root canal therapy is an appropriate treatment option.
Thorough Cleaning
The inside of the tooth is carefully cleaned and disinfected to remove affected tissue and help prepare the root canals for sealing.
Comfort Preparation
Your comfort is a priority. We explain the procedure, address your concerns, and prepare the treatment area before beginning the planned care.
Final Restoration
After treatment, the tooth may require a filling or crown to restore its strength, protect the remaining structure, and support normal chewing function.
Protect What Matters
Restore Comfort While Keeping Your Natural Tooth

A treated tooth still needs consistent care. Brushing, flossing, routine dental visits, and a properly placed restoration all play an important role in protecting the tooth over time. Our team will guide you through the recommended next steps.
